what: Makes the content inside (3D canvas, photos, video) look as if seen through a wet glass pane. The image is blurred twice on a 1/4 buffer, horizontally and vertically with a Gaussian (spread 2.5), so neon becomes round light blobs. Two layers of pooled raindrops that form and dry cell by cell (small 26 cells, large 15 cells) refract (.28) that blurred image, lighting only the drop spots 20% brighter, with darker edges and a bluish tint. Overall brightness .85, edge shadow .75. Raising intensity adds streaks running down and trailing drops. On receiving fx:clear, the glass clears over 1.2s power2.out so the image turns sharp and the pane hides (fx:cleared).

options.intensity: Rain intensity 0~1, default .05 (only pooled drops) — above .4 streaks run down
options.speed: Speed at which droplets form and dry, default 6
options.amount: Initial glass coverage 0–1, default 1 — at 0 it starts cleared and is covered with fx:fog
options.tint: Color multipliers inside the bubble (three), default .85,.92,1.12 at 45% — cool glass
options.[data-fx-part=source]: Picture behind glass — canvas (preserveDrawingBuffer: true for WebGL) · img · video. Cropped with cover when the ratio differs
options.fx:clear · fx:fog: Lift the glass off · cover it again (detail { dur } as length)
options.fx:cleared: Event the element fires after the panel is fully retracted and hidden

use: — On the Enter button, el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('fx:clear'))
note: The original is a three WebGPU post-processing node, so it blends inside the frame that draws the scene. This part is a plate that captures another canvas as a texture every frame and covers it, so it attaches over any image — for a 3D scene, create that renderer with preserveDrawingBuffer: true. The droplet pattern is our own shader that takes the same values (intensity .05, speed 6, blur 2.5, refraction .28, size .45). With no image, nothing is attached
